name: Christel Schaldemose - Proposition de résolution (ensemble du texte)
title: REPORT on the protection of minors online
part_text:
The European Parliament sets out its position on protecting children online. It is not a law: it asks the European Commission to enforce existing rules properly and to propose new ones. It wants a common minimum age of 16 for social media, with parental consent below that, and 13 as an absolute floor. It also asks for safer age checks, a ban on addictive design for minors, and limits on advertising and influencer marketing aimed at children.

- **What changes:** Nothing yet. Parliament asks for new laws, age limits and tougher enforcement.
- **Who it affects:** Children and teenagers, parents, social media and video platforms, game makers, influencers and advertisers.
- **What happens next:** The Commission decides whether to propose legislation; member states must enforce current rules.
